stories.title: Iran vows retaliation as US widens economic sanctions
stories.summary: Iran has promised to retaliate against expanded US economic sanctions, which Washington said would cut off Iran's economic lifeline. Tehran has expressed confidence that major trading partners will resist the US pressure campaign. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled the measures yesterday but stopped short of severe sanctions, saying countries that continued trading with Iran risked being forced out of the dollar-based financial system. "Around the globe, our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone," Mr Bessent told a press conference.

stories.title: Rate of monthly rent rises slowed in Q2 - report
stories.summary: The level of increase in monthly rents slowed in the second quarter of the year, according to a new report from property website Daft. Its Q2 rental report indicates that market rents rose by 1.4% between March and June, which Daft said was "a significant slowdown from the record 4.4% increase in the first quarter and slightly below the average quarterly increase seen over the last decade". It also said rental inflation "remains high in the four major cities outside Dublin". The report shows that market rents in the second quarter were 13% higher year-on-year in Galway city, 12% higher in Cork and up 11% in Limerick.

stories.title: Planned increases in excise duty will not go ahead - Govt
stories.summary: The Government is taking a step-by-step approach to fuel subsidies, Minister for Agriculture Martin Heydon has said, following confirmation that the planned reversal of excise duty fuel cuts in September and October will not go ahead. Earlier, a government spokesperson said that the first two stages of the phased re-introduction of full excise duty fuel costs between 1 September and the start of December will be delayed. In order to do so, the Dáil will be recalled for one day, next Friday, to agree to a financial resolution confirming the matter. He said that the Government is aware of "the impact that the reinstatement of those levies would have had on consumers", but denied that the decision was taken to stave off potential protests.

stories.title: Shein shrinks value to $27 billion, at best, in IPO
stories.summary: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein's valuation has dropped by around 70% from its private market peak four years ago, as it aims to raise up to HK$13.86 billion ($1.77 billion) in its Hong Kong IPO launched today. The long-awaited Hong Kong IPO comes after Shein scrapped plans to list in New York and London over the past four years. It is selling 280 million shares between HK$47.60 and HK$49.50 per share, the filings showed, valuing it at close to $27 billion at the top of that range. Reuters last week exclusively reported the Shein IPO was set to value the company at around a quarter of the $100 billion it was worth in 2022.

stories.title: More than 40,000 evacuate as wildfire nears Reno in US
stories.summary: Authorities in Nevada have urged tens of thousands of people to evacuate and ordered schools to remain closed as a fast-moving, wind-driven wildfire bore down on the western US city of Reno. Around 42,000 people have been forced to evacuate and an additional 45,000 have been told to get ready to leave, Reno Mayor Hillary Schieve told CNN. All but one school in Washoe County, where Reno is located, will remain closed, authorities said. The Hawk Fire began on Saturday and had grown to 6,091 hectares by yesterday evening, showing "extreme fire behavior", according to InciWeb, a US government website that tracks fire activity.

stories.title: McManus: Some county boards view hurling as a 'nuisance'
stories.summary: Former Antrim hurler Neil McManus believes that some county boards regard hurling as a "nuisance" and that counties that ignore the game should be penalised in terms of grants from Croke Park. At the elite level, the 2026 hurling championship was widely viewed as an unsatisfying affair, with an unusually high number of lop-sided games in the Munster championship, culminating in a drab All-Ireland final. While there had been humdrum hurling championships in the past, in 2026 an unflattering light was cast by a newly invigorated football championship, where both the playing rules and the competition format had contributed to one of the most exciting seasons in living memory. Some observers have contended that the commentariat are over-reacting to a single underwhelming campaign but McManus feels the sport has deeper structural issues that need addressing.

stories.summary: Gabriel Martinelli could be set to leave Arsenal for Al Hilal with the two clubs in talks over a transfer. The 25-year-old was not involved in Mikel Arteta's squads for Arsenal’s Community Shield win against Manchester City and their Premier League victory over Coventry. Arteta has spoken to Martinelli about his future with the Gunners exploring a deal to allow him to leave during the window. Saudi Arabian side Al Hilal, who are also reportedly interested in bringing in Ollie Watkins from Aston Villa, want Martinelli with a possible deal in the region of £40million.

stories.title: Munster beat Connacht to extend winning streak to seven
stories.summary: An already-qualified Munster will move on to the Vodafone Women's Interprovincial Championship final in unbeaten form following a 47-12 win away to Connacht. Although Leinster's earlier victory over Ulster ended Connacht's hopes of reaching next week's final at Dexcom Stadium, they put in a gutsy display in their first game in front of the fully-completed Clan Stand. Uillin Eilian had a dream start to her Connacht senior debut, grabbing a third-minute try, but Munster gradually took control of the scoreboard to lead 21-5 at half-time. Alana McInerney's intercept effort was followed by Alisha Flynn driving in under the posts, and then Caitríona Finn's slick 33rd-minute score brought her tally to 11 points.

stories.title: Long-distance love stories: How these couples made it work
stories.summary: Long-distance isn't typically the first choice for those in committed relationships, but what length would you go to maintain a connection while separated by land and sea? Back in June, I sent a letter to Buenos Aires for my partner's 30th birthday. Although I sent it two weeks in advance, thinking it would make it on time, the package still hadn't arrived by mid-August. Obviously, a spiral ensued on my end at missing such a milestone birthday, particularly as he was such a big part of my 30th. It struck me that if we weren’t video-calling each other every day - not to mention sending a steady flow of memes and photo updates - that I would probably have lost some semblance of sanity at never getting a response or explanation.

stories.summary: New EU rules have come into force designed to encourage consumers to repair rather than replace products to tackle the estimated 35 million tonnes of waste the premature disposal of consumer goods generates across the bloc. The 'right to repair' regulations introduce new rights and supports aimed at encouraging repair over disposal, including a repair obligation for manufacturers of certain products and the establishment of a national repair platform to help consumers locate repair services. The rules apply to household and electronic products such as washing machines, vacuum cleaners, mobile phones, and tablets. The regulations are designed to make it easier for consumers to access repair services when products develop faults after the seller's guarantee period.

stories.title: Rise in farm payment schemes to tackle fodder shortages
stories.summary: Payments given to farmers under a number of schemes will see an increase from 70% to 75% as part of a plan to alleviate the effects of fodder shortages. The Department of Agriculture has said both the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) and Complementary Redistributive Income Support for Sustainability scheme (CRISS) will see the increase, as well as the Eco Scheme. Minister for Agriculture Martin Heydon said that rules around the Agri-Climate Rural Environment Scheme (ACRES) will also see more flexibility and will now allow for the mowing of almost 26,000 hectares of land from now, rather than from 31 August. "My department administers €1.6 billion worth of payments over the course of the next four months that farmers expect at a certain set time for the different activities that they're carrying out. And I can't do anything to undermine the scheduling of them or to delay in any way those payments," he said.

stories.summary: Xabi Alonso called on his attacking trio of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro to lead and inspire Chelsea this season after their goals helped begin his tenure began with a 3-2 victory over Fulham at Craven Cottage. On this evidence he will need his forward players to step up and compensate for shortcomings in a jittery, uncertain defence. Chelsea played with a back three, a new shape after last season, and they did not inspire confidence. Fortunately for the manager, his team looked irresistible at times going forward. Joao Pedro scored after 31 seconds from Palmer's pass, and after a Robert Sanchez howler had gifted Josh King an equaliser, they moved through the gears again, Maxence Lacroix bursting forward from the back and setting up £117m signing Rogers before half-time.

stories.title: All Blacks worthy winners as they outscore Springboks
stories.summary: New Zealand overcame a tough physical challenge to outscore South Africa five tries to one and win the first test 33-16 at Ellis Park on Saturday to go one-up in the four-match series. The All Blacks had been underdogs going into the first international of their eight-match tour but took full advantage of the hosts' numerous handling errors and ill discipline for a statement victory that ended a 12-match winning streak for the Springboks and will rock the confidence of the world champions. Will Jordan extended his run as New Zealand's record try scorer with two tries that bookended scores from Josh Moorby, Fabian Holland and Luke Jacobson. Ruben Love kicked over four conversions. South Africa’s try came from Andre Esterhuizen with three penalties and a conversion from Cheslin Kolbe.

stories.title: Dutch broadcaster pulls out of Eurovision 2027
stories.summary: Dutch broadcaster AVROTROS has announced it will not take part in next year's Eurovision Song Contest, saying the event can "no longer be considered neutral" amid divisions surrounding the war in Gaza. AVROTROS, which also boycotted this year’s contest in Vienna, said geopolitical tensions in the Middle East were having a significant impact on Eurovision. "It is undeniable that international conflicts are increasingly affecting the Contest, undermining its neutral character," AVROTROS Director-General Taco Zimmerman said. "The Eurovision Song Contest has therefore become a platform for division."

stories.title: Underground Kerry hot spot wins Bar of the Year 2026
stories.summary: An underground bar in Killarney, Co. Kerry, has taken home the title of 'Bar of the Year' at the 2026 awards. Pig's Lane is a candle-lit haven known for its hand-crafted cocktails, vegan wines, locally sourced snacks and live music, not to mention a whiskey parlour packed with over 400 rare, quality bottles. Founded by Gemma Ring, owner of the O'Donoghue Ring Collection, a family-run Kerry hotel and hospitality group, the award-winning venue has become a popular destination since it opened in 2023. Built on the site of the original Pig’s Lane, a laneway dating back to the 1800s, the subterranean venue can be found within Killarney Towers Hotel on College Street.

stories.title: Uncertainty over Skyclarys decision as HSE team to meet
stories.summary: The Health Service Executive Senior Leadership Team will meet to discuss the drug Skyclarys, which is for people with the rare neurological condition, Friedreich's ataxia. Earlier this month, the HSE Drugs Group met and recommended that the HSE Leadership Team not cover the drug for public patients, essentially on cost grounds. It is unclear whether the HSE Leadership Team will make a final decision on the drug today, or allow more time for talks with the pharmaceutical firm Biogen on the price sought by it. Around 200 people in Ireland are living with the condition and have been campaigning for the drug to be made available by the HSE.

stories.title: TikTok declines Oireachtas call to discuss driving videos
stories.summary: Social media giant TikTok has declined an invitation to appear before the Oireachtas Committee on Media to discuss the posting of videos of people driving down motorways the wrong way and endangering other people's lives. In a response to a meeting request, a TikTok spokesperson said they cannot attend because of the ongoing garda investigation, a separate examination by Coimisiún na Meán and the fact they are the only company to have been asked to attend. Yesterday, Labour TD and media committee chair Alan Kelly wrote to TikTok requesting that its officials attend a meeting next month to discuss the situation and what he described as "content that glorifies irresponsible or illegal activity". "As a result, we believe it would not be possible to appear before the committee in public session until this process is completed.

stories.title: Pioneering UL course sees first master's graduates
stories.summary: A pioneering University of Limerick (UL) software engineering programme, co-designed by global technology company Stripe, is celebrating the graduation of its first master's students today. The first cohort of 16 students from UL's Immersive Software Engineering (ISE) programme will graduate with MSc qualifications before taking up highly sought-after roles with companies including Stripe, Fin, Analog Devices, Shannonside Capital and Amazon Web Services. Stripe has been involved with the programme since its inception, working with UL to co-build the curriculum and develop the industry residency placement process. As a founding partner, the company also played a key role in helping to build the wider network of employers involved in the programme, encouraging other organisations to join what has now become a partnership involving more than 70 companies and organisations.

stories.title: Murphy moving at 'right time' as new WSL season looms
stories.summary: Emily Murphy has the tools to cope with the "big step up" to life with Brighton & Hove Albion as the new Women's Super League season approaches, according to ex-Republic of Ireland international Rachel Graham. Current Girls in Green forward Murphy swapped second tier side Newcastle for Brighton at the end of July and pre-season has been geared to getting ready for the battle for starting places at a club which finished runners-up in last season's Women's FA Cup. The 23-year-old has been one of the star performers for an Ireland side that still has strong aspirations of qualifying for next year's FIFA Women's World Cup. That makes this coming season at Brighton all the more crucial for Murphy as their campaign kicks off in just under a fortnight's time against Arsenal.

stories.title: Feely already dreaming of scaling senior heights in 2027
stories.summary: While the achievements of this year are still very fresh in her mind, Roscommon's Aisling Feely is eagerly anticipating the prospect of playing senior championship football in 2027. Courtesy of their emphatic 2-12 to 0-06 triumph over Fermanagh in the TG4 All-Ireland intermediate football championship decider at Croke Park on 2 August, the Rossies will be one of 12 counties to feature in the top-tier of the LGFA next summer. Even before taking part in the race for the Brendan Martin Cup, the primrose and blue will lock horns with newly-crowned All-Ireland senior winners Galway and Mayo in next year’s Connacht championship at the highest grade of ladies football. This will help to make it a three-team series out in the west once again, as it was when the previous season’s All-Ireland intermediate champions Leitrim made the brief step up to senior football in 2025, and Feely is excited about this new opportunity for Roscommon. "We saw Leitrim do it two years ago. We would have been always there or thereabouts with them. They knocked us out in the quarter-final that year by two points and they went on to win it. That gave us a bit of inspiration. If Leitrim can do it, why can’t we. We’re just as good. To get up to senior is absolutely massive," Feely acknowledged.
